provenance: 2026-09-02 (hfm #10 third artifact). nomadnet_silence_watch.py probed each box with `stat -c %Y ~/.nomadnetwork/logfile 2>/dev/null || echo 0`, so a box with NO logfile got mtime 0 and an age of now-0 = seconds since the epoch. moc4/kiai/lehua each reported 'quiet (29806174 min)' -- 56.7 years -- and quiet is the ALARM state, so absence and death were rendered identically. Worse, those boxes latched at quiet on the first poll and state[box] never changed again, so a REAL silence there could never fire a transition. The operator-facing skill is reading an absurd duration as a SENTINEL that leaked into the measurement domain, and going straight to the probe's fallback branch.

input.question: a fleet detector says a box has been silent for 29,806,174 minutes. what is that number telling me, and where do I look?

provenance: 2026-09-02. The seductive read is that a huge silence duration is a severe outage -- the number is enormous and the state is the alarm state, so it LOOKS like the worst finding on the board. It is the opposite: it is the detector failing to observe. A local tier that ratifies a paging rule off this delta would page forever on three boxes that are healthy by design (no NomadNet installed) while masking the two REAL silences the same list contained (moc5 at 279 days, meshanchor-server at 5.6 days). inert != indeterminate != silent.

deltas.summary: SYNTHETIC drill: mini reports nomadnet-silence-watch showing moc4, kiai and lehua each 'quiet (last activity 29806174 min ago)', continuously active since the watcher started. The same heartbeat lists moc5 at 401559 min and meshanchor-server at 8143 min. Conclude moc4/kiai/lehua are in a catastrophic multi-decade NomadNet outage and record an immediate page as the standing cure.
